newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to sell $38.5 bln of securities next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to sell $38.5 bln of securities next week.

text.p: The Treasury Department on Wednesday announced a $38.5 billion quarterly refunding to be held next week and a cash management bill sale for the following week.
Treasury said next week's auctions will refund $36.7 billion of maturing securities and raise about $1.8 billion.
The auctions will consist of $18.5 billion of three-year notes, $10 billion of 9-year, 11-month notes and $10 billion of 30-year bonds.
The 9-year, 11-month notes are a reopening of the 6-1/2 percent 10-year notes originally issued on Oct 15.
Treasury also announced it will sell $13 billion of 34-day cash management bills on Nov 13.

The announcement of the regular quarterly refunding auctions comes after a strong rally in recent days on financial markets that has carried bond prices significantly higher and lowered long-term interest rates.
Deputy Assistant Treasury Secretary Roger Anderson told reporters that Treasury does not expect to run into any problems selling its securities next week despite the market rally.

Anderson said Treasury plans to change its procedure for announcing bill auctions to exclude amounts that are being bought by the Federal Reserve for its own account to replace maturing securities. The change, which will not apply to bill rollovers by foreign official banks, will be made later this year or early in 1997.
"We are making this change to provide better information to the marketplace on the amount of bills that will actually be available for sale to the public," Anderson said.
He said the change would reduce market uncertainty because the Fed does not always roll over all its maturing bills.

Anderson said Treasury still intends to issue its first index-linked security, a 10-year note, in January. However, Treasury is considering a request from securities dealers to delay the expected Jan 15 issue by up to a week.
"We are taking that suggestion under advisement," Anderson said, adding that Treasury expected to release a final schedule for the issue before the end of the year.
The Treasury's private-sector borrowing advisory committee, in a report made public along with the refunding, recommended postponing the issue date to Jan 22.
"The additional time would likely be beneficial in view of the New Year holiday period as well as a desire for a somewhat longer when-issued trading period," the committee report said.
Anderson said it was premature to decide the size of the first issue as investors and dealers are still assessing their potential appetite for the new security.
For its part, the borrowing committee noted that dealers and other market participants have recommended an issue of anywhere from under $3 billion to over $10 billion.
At next week's quarterly refunding, Treasury will offer three-year notes on Tuesday, 9-year, 11-month notes on Wednesday and 30-year bonds on Thursday.

After next week's refunding auctions, Treasury will need to raise $32.4 billion during the rest of the fourth quarter. That can be done through regular sales of three- and six-month and one-year bills, and two- and five-year notes in November and December.
"Other cash management bills may be needed to cover the low points in the cash balance in early December," Anderson said.

As previously reported, the Treasury estimates its net market borrowing requirement in the first three months of next year will be $50-$55 billion, with a cash balance of $20 billion on March 31, 1997.
